categories.main_business_segments: Perrigo operates two main business segments: Consumer Self-Care Americas (CSCA), which covers the U.S. and Canada, and Consumer Self-Care International (CSCI), which includes operations primarily in Europe and Australia. The company previously had an Rx (prescription pharmaceuticals) segment, but this has been divested and is now reported as discontinued operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Perrigo's core capabilities center on the development, manufacturing, and marketing of over-the-counter (OTC) self-care products, including both branded and store brand (private label) offerings. The company utilizes advanced R&D for product formulation, regulatory compliance, and manufacturing across multiple dosage forms and packaging types, supported by a global supply chain and 17 manufacturing plants. Innovation includes Rx-to-OTC switches, product reformulation, and line extensions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Perrigo primarily serves major global, national, and regional retail drug, supermarket, and mass merchandise chains, e-commerce stores, and wholesalers. Its key markets are OTC health and wellness, nutrition (infant formula), oral care, pain relief, skin care, women's health, and vitamins/minerals/supplements, with a strong presence in both branded and store brand product categories.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally, with primary revenue generated in North America (U.S. and Canada) and Europe, and additional presence in Australia and select other international markets. Perrigo has manufacturing, R&D, and logistics facilities in the U.S., U.K., Belgium, France, Germany, Austria, China, and Australia, and sells products in more than 29 countries.
categories.supply_chain_position: Perrigo is positioned downstream in the supply chain, focusing on the development, manufacturing, and distribution of finished consumer self-care products. The company manages a complex supply chain, sourcing raw materials and packaging components, and delivering finished goods to retailers, wholesalers, and pharmacies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Perrigo's strategic focus is on sustainable, value-accretive growth through consumer-preferred brands and innovation, category growth, supply chain excellence, and operational efficiency. Key initiatives include the Supply Chain Reinvention Program, Project Energize, and ongoing investment in R&D for new product development, Rx-to-OTC switches, and sustainability (e.g., reducing emissions and improving packaging recyclability).
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of OTC self-care products, both branded and store brand, to retailers, wholesalers, and pharmacies. Additional revenue streams include contract manufacturing, licensing, and distribution agreements, as well as royalty income from supply and distribution deals.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Perrigo faces competition from both generic and branded pharmaceutical and consumer health companies, including Dr. Reddy's, LNK International, PL Developments, Aurobindo, Sun Pharmaceuticals, Haleon, Kenvue, Procter & Gamble, Reckitt Benckiser, Abbott Nutrition, Bayer, Sanofi, Philips, Teva, Viatris, Stada, and Novartis. Perrigo is a leading provider of store brand OTC products in North America and has a strong branded portfolio in Europe, positioning itself as a pure-play self-care company.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Perrigo reported net sales of $4.66 billion, up 4.6% from the prior year, with a gross profit of $1.68 billion (36.1% margin). The company has over 9,100 employees and a global asset base exceeding $10.8 billion. Growth is driven by acquisitions (e.g., HRA Pharma, Gateway infant formula), innovation, and supply chain initiatives, though profitability has been impacted by restructuring, inflation, and regulatory costs.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Perrigo's value proposition lies in providing high-quality, affordable self-care products that are accessible without a prescription, offering both branded and store brand options across a broad product spectrum. The company differentiates itself through its scale, first-to-market product development, regulatory expertise, and ability to deliver comparable quality to national brands at lower prices, supporting both consumer value and retailer profitability.
